newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Bolger says poll result not "Bloody Sunday".
newsitem.headline: NZ's Bolger says poll result not "Bloody Sunday".

text.p: Prime Minister Jim Bolger said his message to financial markets was that the inconclusive outcome of New Zealand's general election was not the "Sunday, bloody Sunday" he had warned of.
Bolger had warned during his campaign that a lurch to the left could roll back aspects of New Zealand's free-market reforms and bring economic turmoil.

"That has not turned out to be so, because it's clear the left did not get the vote that was possible. We could have done considerable damage to New Zealand. I don't see that happening," Bolger told reporters in his home constituency of Te Kuiti.

"I don't see those policies coming through, so the vote was not for that. I think we can relax a little on this Sunday, not totally remove all worry. We can relax so we can put together a sensible government that will keep New Zealand moving."

Bolger and Labour Party leader Helen Clark have both said they aim to lead the next government after results gave the conservative National Party 44 seats and Labour 37 in a new 120-member parliament.
Economic nationalist New Zealand First holds the balance of power with 17 seats and has not said which way it will lean.
Bolger has not ruled out a minority government with radical free-market Act New Zealand (eight seats) and the sole MP from the centrist United Party.
